Workflow design / October 2026

The SOP is part of the architecture

Before choosing the agent, understand the decisions, handoffs, and exceptions in the work.

When a team asks for an AI workflow, my first question is about the work itself. What starts it? Who makes the decision? What information do they need? Where does the process stall?

Those questions are architectural. A model can help interpret an input, but the surrounding workflow still needs clear ownership, inputs, outputs, and a useful next action. An undocumented process makes those decisions harder to see.

That is why workflow mapping and SOP improvement come before the assisted build in the AI Capability Ladder I use at Clarity Works. The process gives the build its shape. It also gives the team something concrete to question and improve.

I want a working session to leave behind more than a promising demo. The team should be able to explain what the workflow does, recognize when it needs human judgment, and maintain the process as the work changes.

For me, discovery and engineering belong in the same conversation. Understanding the process is how I decide what is worth building.
